CVE-2026-118423.description: The WP Libre Form WordPress plugin 1.5.0.1 does not validate the type of files uploaded through its form submissions, allowing unauthenticated attackers to upload PHP files to a web-accessible location and execute them, leading to remote code execution.
CVE-2026-118423.summary_ko: WP Libre Form 1.5.0.1 플러그인에서 파일 업로드 시 형식을 검증하지 않아, 인증되지 않은 공격자가 PHP 파일을 업로드하고 원격 코드 실행을 시도할 수 있는 취약점이 발견되었습니다.

curation.reason_ko: 워드프레스 플러그인에서 인증되지 않은 사용자가 PHP 파일을 업로드하여 원격 코드 실행이 가능한 치명적인 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-116779.description: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.3, sofia_presence_handle_sip_i_message() split the To user of an inbound SIP MESSAGE on a plus sign and treated the left side as a chat protocol selector. Selecting the api chat proto reached switch_api_execute(), allowing a peer whose MESSAGE was accepted to run FreeSWITCH API commands, including operating-system command sinks, with the daemon's privileges. Inbound chat is enabled on the stock internal and external profiles, and any authenticated profile account is sufficient; stock directory users without password material can also remove that barrier in affected configurations. The flaw permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution, and exploitation has been observed in the wild. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.3.
CVE-2026-116779.summary_ko: FreeSWITCH의 SIP 메시지 처리 과정에서 적절한 입력값 검증이 이루어지지 않아 인증된 사용자가 임의의 API 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: FreeSWITCH의 SIP 메시지 처리 오류로 인증 없이 원격에서 시스템 명령을 실행할 수 있어 위험도가 매우 높습니다.

CVE-2026-123198.description: LMFDB before commit 01829bd contains a server-side template injection vulnerability in the render_knowl function that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject Jinja expressions via request parameters. Attackers can supply crafted query-string values or 'content' data to /knowledge/render/<ID> to reach Python builtins and execute operating system commands as the web application account.
CVE-2026-123198.summary_ko: LMFDB의 render_knowl 함수에서 서버 사이드 템플릿 주입 취약점이 발견되어 원격 공격자가 운영체제 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: LMFDB의 템플릿 주입 취약점으로 인해 원격 공격자가 운영체제 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-54143.description: OpenHuman is an open-source agent harness available as a desktop application and Rust library. Before version 0.57.13, an attacker who can send messages to a configured external channel can cause the agent to create persistent shell cron jobs without human approval. The scheduler later executes these jobs with the privileges of the OpenHuman runtime user. Command validation also permits leading environment assignments that can redirect allowed commands to executable helpers. The demonstrated exploit requires a suitable helper executable already present on the host. This can lead to unauthorized persistent command execution and compromise data and resources accessible to OpenHuman. This issue is fixed in version 0.57.13.
CVE-2026-54143.summary_ko: OpenHuman에서 외부 채널 메시지를 통해 승인되지 않은 셸 작업이 생성 및 실행될 수 있으며 환경 변수 조작으로 명령 수행이 가능합니다.

curation.reason_ko: OpenHuman에서 셸 작업 생성을 통해 인증되지 않은 공격자가 임의의 명령을 실행할 수 있는 취약점이 확인되었습니다.

CVE-2026-119757.description: BTCPay Server before 2.4.2, including 2.4.2 release candidates, contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to retrieve .macaroon credential files for an LND (Lightning Network Daemon) node. Attackers can use the exposed macaroon to gain full control of the LND node, including moving funds, resulting in theft of funds from affected deployments.
CVE-2026-119757.summary_ko: BTCPay Server에서 인증되지 않은 원격 공격자가 LND 노드 접속을 위한 중요 인증 파일을 탈취하여 자금 도난을 일으킬 수 있는 정보 노출 취약점입니다.

curation.reason_ko: BTCPay Server에서 LND 인증 파일을 탈취해 자금을 도난할 수 있는 심각한 정보 노출 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-102940.description: OpenEMR is a free and open source electronic health records and medical practice management application. Prior to 8.4.0, controllers/C_Document.class.php write actions, including move_action_process(), do not verify the caller's access to the source document, current patient and category, or destination patient and category before Document::change_patient() performs the mutation. A low-privilege authenticated user can reassign an arbitrary document to a patient or category the user can access and then retrieve it through the normally protected read path. The reassignment occurs before a later list rendering check, so a final HTTP 403 response does not mean the unauthorized write was blocked. This issue is fixed in version 8.4.0.
CVE-2026-102940.summary_ko: OpenEMR 8.4.0 이전 버전의 문서 관리 기능에서 접근 권한을 확인하지 않고 문서를 재할당하는 문제가 발생합니다. 이로 인해 낮은 권한의 인증된 사용자가 임의의 문서를 자신이 접근 가능한 범주로 옮겨 조회할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: OpenEMR에서 의료 기록에 대한 무단 접근 및 재할당이 가능한 심각한 권한 관리 결함입니다.

CVE-2026-100358.description: SuiteCRM is an open-source, enterprise-ready Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software application. Prior to 7.15.2 and 8.10.2, the Studio Dropdown Editor passes $dropdown_name through html_entity_decode() and writes the result verbatim into a PHP language file under custom/ that is included on later page loads. An administrator can inject persistent PHP that executes as the web-server account, survives cache clears, and compromises application and host confidentiality, integrity, and availability. This issue is fixed in versions 7.15.2 and 8.10.2.
CVE-2026-100358.summary_ko: SuiteCRM의 Studio Dropdown Editor에서 입력값 검증 미흡으로 인해 관리자가 임의의 PHP 코드를 삽입하여 실행할 수 있는 취약점이 발견되었습니다.

curation.reason_ko: SuiteCRM에서 관리자가 임의의 PHP 코드를 삽입하여 실행할 수 있는 원격 코드 실행 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-63017.description: Incorrect authorization in PowerSYSTEM Center allows a low-privileged, authenticated user to access resources normally limited to administrators.
CVE-2026-63017.summary_ko: PowerSYSTEM Center의 권한 부여 로직 오류로 인해 일반 사용자가 관리자 전용 리소스에 접근할 수 있는 취약점입니다.

curation.reason_ko: PowerSYSTEM Center의 권한 부여 로직 오류로 인해 일반 사용자가 관리자 전용 리소스에 접근할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-88800.description: The MDJM Event Management and Mobile Events Manager WordPress plugins through 1.7.8.7 act on a role deletion request on every page load with no capability check and no nonce, and the guard meant to protect roles that have users assigned reads a different part of the request from the one that selects what is deleted, allowing unauthenticated attackers to remove any WordPress role including administrator, which permanently strips every user of their capabilities.
CVE-2026-88800.summary_ko: MDJM Event Management 및 Mobile Events Manager 1.7.8.7 이하 버전에서 권한 삭제 요청 시 검증 절차가 미흡하여, 인증되지 않은 공격자가 관리자 권한을 포함한 모든 워드프레스 사용자 역할을 임의로 삭제할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: 워드프레스 플러그인에서 인증되지 않은 사용자가 관리자 역할을 제거할 수 있는 치명적인 권한 탈취 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-119344.description: Cocos AI is a confidential computing system for AI. In version 0.8.2 and earlier, Cocos AI accepts trusted execution environment attestation Evidence when firmware patch levels and software measurements match, without binding the Evidence to an allowed platform owner or unique machine identity and without enforcing revocation. A remote attacker who controls or compromises another platform trusted by the same verifier can substitute valid Evidence from that platform and cause authorization of the wrong platform. This vulnerability is addressed in 0.9.0. However, this vulnerability can't be patched in source code alone, since the vulnerability arises from the confidential computing threat model itself.
CVE-2026-119344.summary_ko: Cocos AI는 신뢰 실행 환경 증명 과정에서 고유 식별자나 해지 검증이 미흡하여 외부 공격자가 유효한 증명 데이터를 도용할 위험이 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Cocos AI의 증명 데이터 검증 미흡으로 인해 유효한 증명 데이터를 도용하여 잘못된 플랫폼 인증이 발생할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-85076.description: Cronicle is a multi-server task scheduler and runner, with a web based front-end UI. Prior to 0.9.124, an authenticated non-admin with run_events, create_events, or edit_events privilege can supply undeclared keys in event params through api_create_event, api_update_event, or api_run_event. lib/api.js and lib/api/event.js validate the parameter object without restricting its keys, and lib/job.js uppercases those keys and applies them to the child process environment after administrator-defined plugin variables. A key that collides with a security-sensitive environment variable can therefore override the plugin execution context and may cause privilege escalation, arbitrary code execution, data access, or service disruption depending on the plugin and runtime. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.124.
CVE-2026-85076.summary_ko: Cronicle에서 이벤트 파라미터 검증이 미흡하여, 공격자가 환경 변수를 덮어쓰고 권한 상승이나 임의 코드 실행을 유도할 수 있는 취약점입니다.

curation.reason_ko: Cronicle에서 이벤트 파라미터 검증 미흡으로 환경 변수를 덮어쓰고 권한 상승이나 임의 코드 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-114134.description: Black is the uncompromising Python code formatter. Prior to 26.10.1, the Black GitHub Action with use_pyproject: true accepts tool.black.required-version from pyproject.toml without validating that it is a released Black version specifier. An attacker who can submit a pull request can change that field to a direct reference to attacker-controlled code, causing the workflow to install and execute the code in the victim repository's GitHub Actions context. This issue is fixed in version 26.10.1.
CVE-2026-114134.summary_ko: Black GitHub Action에서 pyproject.toml의 버전 정보를 검증하지 않아 공격자가 임의의 코드를 설치하고 실행할 수 있는 취약점입니다.

curation.reason_ko: Black GitHub Action에서 버전 정보를 검증하지 않아 공격자가 임의의 코드를 설치하고 실행할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-104269.description: ModSecurity is an open source, cross platform web application firewall (WAF) engine for Apache, IIS and Nginx. From 3.0.0 until 3.0.17, ModSecurity's multipart parser does not apply the RFC 2231 filename* parameter precedence used by common Go, Python, Node.js, and Java application parsers. A Content-Disposition header can provide a benign filename parameter for ModSecurity and a different encoded filename* value that the backend prefers, causing MULTIPART_FILENAME rules and the application to make security decisions on different names. Applications that use the backend-selected name for storage, extension checks, or content-type inference can therefore receive a filename that bypassed WAF inspection. PHP's native multipart parser is not affected by this discrepancy. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.17.
CVE-2026-104269.summary_ko: ModSecurity의 멀티파트 파서가 RFC 2231 파일명 매개변수 우선순위를 올바르게 처리하지 못합니다. 공격자가 조작된 Content-Disposition 헤더를 보내 WAF 검사를 우회하여 백엔드 애플리케이션에 파일을 전달할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: ModSecurity의 파일명 처리 오류로 WAF 검사를 우회하여 악성 파일을 백엔드에 전달할 수 있는 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-123158.description: sshd in OpenSSH before 10.6p2 on Linux, when musl libc is used without PAM, lacks a workaround for a password authentication bypass (related to misinterpretation of whether a string is intended to be a password hash). For some configurations of accounts, any password between 256 and 1024 characters succeeds. An example of a platform using musl libc without PAM is Alpine Linux.
CVE-2026-123158.summary_ko: Linux 환경에서 musl libc를 사용하는 OpenSSH는 비밀번호 해시 해석 오류로 인해 특정 조건에서 인증 우회가 발생할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: OpenSSH의 특정 리눅스 환경에서 인증 우회가 가능한 취약점으로 보안 영향이 큽니다.

CVE-2026-112208.description: A flaw was found in the Organization identity-first login flow of the Keycloak authentication server. Keycloak is an open-source identity and access management solution used to secure modern applications and services. The issue occurs when an attacker who belongs to multiple organizations initiates a login and then switches to a registration or password reset path. During this process, a flag indicating a successful login is not properly cleared when the user is removed from the session. An attacker can then provide a victim's username, and the system incorrectly treats the stale flag as proof of the victim's identity. This allows the attacker to bypass authentication and gain full access to the victim's account and connected applications.
CVE-2026-112208.summary_ko: Keycloak의 로그인 흐름 중 사용자 세션 정리 오류로 인해 공격자가 다른 사용자의 계정 권한을 탈취하여 접근할 수 있는 취약점입니다.

curation.reason_ko: Keycloak의 로그인 흐름 중 세션 처리 오류로 다른 사용자의 계정 권한을 탈취할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-119083.description: Path traversal in the archive extraction utility in GluonTS before 0.17.0 might allow an actor who supplies a crafted tar archive to write arbitrary files outside the intended extraction directory with the privileges of the extracting process via symbolic or hard links contained in the archive. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.17.0 or later.
CVE-2026-119083.summary_ko: GluonTS의 아카이브 추출 도구에서 경로 탐색 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 조작된 tar 파일을 통해 압축 해제 프로세스의 권한으로 의도된 디렉터리 외부의 파일을 임의로 작성할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: GluonTS 아카이브 추출 도구에서 경로 탐색을 통해 의도된 외부 파일을 임의로 작성할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-102523.description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.11.1 until 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, ALTER TABLE ... CONVERT ... PARTITION does not apply filename encoding to user-specified partition names before using them in filesystem path construction. An authenticated database user can use a partition name requiring filename escaping to make the conversion operate on table files the user is not authorized to access, allowing unauthorized table reads or modifications. This issue is fixed in versions 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.
CVE-2026-102523.summary_ko: MariaDB 서버의 파티션 이름 처리 방식에서 파일명 인코딩 누락으로 인해, 인증된 사용자가 허가되지 않은 테이블 파일에 접근하거나 수정할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: MariaDB의 파티션 이름 처리 오류로 인해 인증된 사용자가 허가되지 않은 파일에 접근할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-123208.description: noname Electron desktop build v1.11.2 through v1.11.6.1 contains an unauthenticated local file server with wildcard CORS that allows malicious websites to read, overwrite, or delete installation files. Attackers can send cross-origin requests to /writeFile on localhost port 8089 to overwrite renderer scripts, executing JavaScript with Node.js access as the local user.
CVE-2026-123208.summary_ko: noname Electron 데스크톱 빌드의 로컬 파일 서버가 취약한 CORS 설정을 사용하여, 외부 공격자가 로컬 파일을 조작하고 JavaScript를 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Electron 데스크톱 애플리케이션에서 파일 서버의 CORS 설정 취약점으로 로컬 파일을 조작할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-119744.description: Cendio ThinLinc contains an improper authentication vulnerability in its browser-based web client (tlwebaccess) that allows an authenticated attacker to impersonate any other user, including root, by exploiting flaws in multi-step authentication flows such as one-time passwords, login banners, or expired password prompts. Attackers can leverage this authentication bypass during the multi-step login process to gain unauthorized access to other user accounts, including administrative privileges, in versions from 4.1.0 through 4.20.0.
CVE-2026-119744.summary_ko: Cendio ThinLinc의 웹 클라이언트(tlwebaccess) 다단계 인증 과정에서 결함이 발견되었습니다. 인증된 공격자가 이를 악용해 루트 권한을 포함한 타인 계정으로 가장하고 무단 접근할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Cendio ThinLinc의 다단계 인증 결함으로 공격자가 루트 권한을 포함한 타인 계정으로 가장할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-111494.description: Incorrect validation of TLS certificates in the MatchPoint Android app due to a TrustManager that accepts any certificate and a permissive hostname validator. Additionally, the app allows unencrypted HTTP traffic. An attacker capable of intercepting the victim's traffic could read and modify communications, including credentials and personal data.
CVE-2026-111494.summary_ko: MatchPoint 안드로이드 앱이 TLS 인증서 검증을 올바르게 수행하지 않고 암호화되지 않은 HTTP 통신을 허용합니다. 공격자는 이를 악용해 사용자의 트래픽을 가로채고 계정 정보 및 개인 데이터를 탈취하거나 변조할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: MatchPoint Android 앱에서 TLS 인증서 검증 미흡으로 통신 데이터가 가로채기 당하거나 수정될 수 있습니다.

c10dac4f31c2500c2b09333c.title_original: “AI 시대 보안 전략 공유"...AIS 2026, 보안담당자 700여 명 참석 성황리 개최
c10dac4f31c2500c2b09333c.excerpt: 인공지능(AI)이 사이버 공격과 방어 기술을 빠르게 바꾸는 가운데, 보안담당자들이 한자리에 모여 새로운 위협과 실무 대응 전략을 공유했다.데일리시큐가 주최하고 한국인터넷진흥원(KISA)과 한국정보보호산업협회(KISIA)가 후원한 ‘2026 인공지능 보안 컨퍼런스(AIS 2026)’가 11월 3일 서울 한국과학기술회관 국제회의실에서 700여 명의 보안담당자와 관계자가 참여한 가운데 성황리에 개최됐다.‘AI 시대, 사이버위협과 대응방안 공유’를 주제로 열린 이번 행사는 총 10개 발표와 기업 전시를 통해 AI 기반 공격의 변화, 기업의
c10dac4f31c2500c2b09333c.summary_ko: 지난 11월 3일 개최된 AIS 2026은 700여 명의 보안 담당자가 참석해 AI 기반 공격 및 방어 전략을 공유했습니다. 설문 결과 보안 담당자들은 AI 도입 시 기업 정보 유출을 가장 크게 우려하며, 향후 AI 보안관제 자동화 기술에 높은 관심을 보였습니다.

curation.reason_ko: AIS 2026 컨퍼런스를 통해 AI 시대의 사이버 위협과 실무 대응 전략이 활발히 논의되었습니다.

b5828fee436e51acc4e6d2bd.title_original: 퓨쳐시스템, Node.js 취약점 4건 대응…위가디아 통합관리 제품 업데이트 제공
b5828fee436e51acc4e6d2bd.excerpt: 네트워크 보안 전문기업 퓨쳐시스템(대표 정원규)은 노드제이에스(Node.js) 관련 보안 취약점 4건에 대응하기 위해 자사 위가디아(WeGuardia) 통합관리 제품에 보안 업데이트를 제공한다고 밝혔다.이번 대응 대상은 CVE-2026-111497, CVE-2026-105482, CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069다. 회사는 해당 취약점이 제품에 미치는 영향을 검토하고, 보안 조치를 반영한 업데이트를 지원한다고 설명했다.Node.js는 서버와 애플리케이션 구동에 활용되는 소프트웨어 실행 환경이다. 이를 사용하
b5828fee436e51acc4e6d2bd.title_ko: 퓨쳐시스템, 위가디아 통합관리 제품의 Node.js 취약점 업데이트 제공
b5828fee436e51acc4e6d2bd.summary_ko: 퓨쳐시스템은 위가디아 통합관리 제품에 영향을 주는 Node.js 관련 취약점 4건(CVE-2026-111497 등)에 대한 보안 업데이트를 배포했습니다. 회사는 보안 장비를 통합 관리하는 시스템의 안전성을 위해 이번 조치를 시행했다고 밝혔습니다. 자세한 적용 방법은 공식 파트너사를 통해 확인할 수 있습니다.

992b1d86b20f78fc0f9587e1.title_original: Dharma Field Extractor: Any Document In, Structured Fields in JSON Out
992b1d86b20f78fc0f9587e1.title_ko: Dharma Field Extractor: 다양한 문서에서 구조화된 JSON 데이터 추출 모델
992b1d86b20f78fc0f9587e1.summary_ko: Dharma AI 팀이 출시한 20억 개의 파라미터 모델로, 계약서나 인보이스 등 다양한 문서에서 사용자가 정의한 스키마에 맞춰 정확한 구조화된 JSON 필드를 추출합니다. 기존 범용 LLM보다 저렴한 비용으로 특정 문서 작업에 최적화된 높은 성능을 제공합니다.

612ca69014761454cd790d03.title_original: Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root
612ca69014761454cd790d03.title_ko: Debian 및 Ubuntu APT 취약점, 패키지 변조 및 루트 권한 실행 위험
612ca69014761454cd790d03.summary_ko: Debian 및 Ubuntu의 패키지 관리자 APT에서 중간자 공격(MitM)을 통해 검증된 패키지를 악성 패키지로 교체하고 루트 권한을 탈취할 수 있는 심각한 취약점이 발견되었습니다(CVE-2026-109518). 해당 취약점은 패키지 다운로드 재시도 기능의 로직 오류로 인해 발생하며, 관련 배포판들은 보안 패치를 배포 중입니다.

curation.reason_ko: Debian 및 Ubuntu의 패키지 관리자 APT에서 중간자 공격으로 루트 권한 탈취가 가능한 심각한 취약점이 발견되었습니다.

68a5ed98b2519d98e83e9ece.title_original: SonicWall Won't Patch EoL GMS Flaws That Could Expose Files, Alter Database Records
68a5ed98b2519d98e83e9ece.title_ko: SonicWall, 지원 종료된 GMS 제품의 취약점 패치 미제공 결정
68a5ed98b2519d98e83e9ece.summary_ko: 소닉월(SonicWall)은 보안 취약점 CVE-2026-109593 및 CVE-2026-109594가 발견된 GMS(Global Management System) 9.5.2 이하 버전에 대해 제품 지원 종료를 이유로 패치를 제공하지 않겠다고 발표했습니다. 해당 취약점은 각각 파일 읽기 및 SQL 인젝션 공격이 가능합니다. 소닉월은 보안 위험을 방지하기 위해 네트워크 보안 관리자(NSM)로 업그레이드할 것을 권고했습니다.

5e5aaa012c5e04e4c1a9f5df.title_original: Researchers Uncover Prompt Adware Hidden in OpenAI Codex Jailbreak Toolkit
5e5aaa012c5e04e4c1a9f5df.title_ko: OpenAI Codex 탈옥 툴킷에 포함된 '프롬프트 애드웨어' 발견
5e5aaa012c5e04e4c1a9f5df.summary_ko: 체크포인트 리서치는 OpenAI Codex의 설정을 변조하여 광고를 삽입하는 '프롬프트 애드웨어' 하이오우(Haiou)를 발견했습니다. 이 툴킷은 사용자의 AI 에이전트 명령을 수정하여 타사 AI 게이트웨이 서비스로 유도합니다. 이는 단순한 광고 노출을 넘어 AI 에이전트를 이용한 공급망 공격으로 이어질 수 있어 주의가 필요합니다.

curation.reason_ko: OpenAI Codex 툴킷 내 프롬프트 애드웨어 삽입이 확인되어 AI 에이전트 공급망 보안 위협이 대두되었습니다.

e45ae4601ad6c35615d4e345.title_original: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
e45ae4601ad6c35615d4e345.excerpt: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder’s web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016. The security firm Layer3 Intel said it detected multiple residential proxy nodes beaconing out from the internet address network reserved for the Executive Office of the President ( AS2650 ). Layer3 said the proxy activity was relatively persistent between October 5 to November 3, and that a review of the proxies available from AS2650 showed they exited from the White House network 236 times during that period. The proxy tracking company Synthient said on Twitter/X that the activity it saw coming from AS2650 was related to multiple Windows 11 installations of a service called Infatica , a proxy program that is often integrated into “free” mobile and desktop applications . Infatica’s founder Vladimir Fomenko is a Russian man whose hosting firm King Servers was home to six of the eight internet addresses used by Russia’s state security services to compromise databases for election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016. 9c59984f3c0e963d7900da87.title_original: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
9c59984f3c0e963d7900da87.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. Yet a reviewer can both repair errors and replace decisions that were already correct. We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding? We compare broad override authority with an evidence gate that permits replacement only after the reviewer produces a mechanically valid record of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. Across two locally run open-weight models, 96 spatial-policy tasks, and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark, the gate sharply reduces corruption of correct proposals while retaining most repairs of violations. The directions of this tradeoff are partly implied by the rule; its magnitude depends on reviewer transitions and upstream proposal states. A prospective validation then gives the reviewer an explicit choice to retain, replace, or escalate. This eliminates correct-proposal corruption for Qwen, but Mistral still replaces all 48 correct proposals; Qwen also declines every welfare-only repair that Mistral frequently attempts. Thus interface design changes reviewer behavior but is not a model-independent safeguard. The result is not that restricted review is universally better. 28fbe6fc48a4810cc00ceee4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool descriptions tell an agent what an action can do, but they do not necessarily reveal whether that action is healthy or suitable at the moment of use. Execution harnesses often possess this information through monitors, traces, and recent failures while the model choosing the next action does not. We call this gap operational blindness. We introduce Agent Harness Awareness, a trust-separated design in which the host supplies a small, fresh, verified state snapshot before a consequential action while retaining measurement, enforcement, evaluation, and final dispatch authority. We test its tools-and-network instance with ToolRoute, a controlled isolation benchmark that holds the task and candidate semantics constant and varies the operational information available to the model. In a 216-decision ablation across GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, and Gemini 3.7 Flash, verified tool-health state reduced mean observable policy regret by 96.9% against a same-shape neutral control (4,252 ms to 131 ms) and raised single-dispatch completion from 69.4% to 95.8%. In a separate 27-decision end-to-end replication with live local TCP/HTTP execution, OpenTelemetry client spans, and Toxiproxy-injected faults, verified state reduced mean regret from 8,956 ms to 0 ms (zero excess observable operational cost) and completed the live action in 9/9 model-by-fault cases versus 5/9 for the neutral control. d6a404a03a0858ac654e0b66.title_original: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
d6a404a03a0858ac654e0b66.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems powered by large language models (LLMs) execute as autonomous multi-step pipelines that dynamically invoke tools, integrate observations into memory, and iterate until a task is resolved or a resource budget is exhausted. Unlike classical workflows with fixed graphs, the aggregate compute, bandwidth, and end-to-end latency demands of such pipelines are unknown at dispatch time: they emerge at runtime from intermediate observations and stochastic token sampling, yielding heavy-tailed, multi-modal random variables. This unpredictability forces infrastructure orchestrators into a dilemma: under-provisioning risks mid-execution throttling and deadline violations, while over-provisioning wastes scarce edge or cloud capacity. Existing schedulers require a fully known pipeline graph, while edge resource-management methods rely on parametric or stationary demand models, and neither fits the unknown, non-stationary profiles of agentic pipelines. We formalize this setting as the uncertainty-aware agentic orchestration problem, where the goal is to reserve, at dispatch time, compute and bandwidth allocations that cover actual pipeline demands, and to verify that the pipeline can meet its deadline, each with a prescribed probability. We then propose Conformal Reservation for Orchestration (CRO), an online algorithm that translates a sliding window of past execution traces into dispatch-time resou

170913d7e0d53c10fd34a5f7.title_original: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
170913d7e0d53c10fd34a5f7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. We propose challenge-aware adaptive recruitment: an external CHALLENGER inspects the evolving reasoning trace and identifies specific factual or expertise gaps. These signals trigger targeted knowledge retrieval or mid-discussion specialist recruitment. On the MEDAGENTSBENCH hard subset (862 questions across nine biomedical datasets), upfront retrieval provides little benefit, while challenge-aware in-between retrieval performs better; on a multi-specialist backbone it improves accuracy on 8 of 9 datasets and adds 6 percentage points over Challenger Only. Ablations indicate benefits from both retrieval timing and gap-specific query signals, and a live web-search experiment shows that the timing advantage persists across retrieval backends. For specialist recruitment, self-triggered adaptation is unreliable, whereas Challenger-triggered recruitment raises GPT-4.1-mini MedQA accuracy from 46% to 54%, with positive direction on all tested generalization datasets. bbce8b50c6f057c7a77de1e2.title_original: A Feasibility Condition for Confidence-Gated Tiered LLM Inference
bbce8b50c6f057c7a77de1e2.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tiered inference distributes large language model computation across a hierarchy of devices, from on-device and edge hardware to the datacenter, and is increasingly offered as the route to cheaper, lower-latency, and more private serving. Most such systems orchestrate frozen model checkpoints, and most decide what to resolve locally and what to escalate using a confidence signal produced by a forward-deployed model. We give a closed-form condition for when no threshold on that signal makes a tiered cascade worthwhile relative to sending every query to the backstop. Modeling the routing decision as a binary test and separating local from escalation cost through an architecture cost ratio $\kappa$, we derive a feasibility condition bracketed by a signal-free floor, below which a cascade is feasible at any signal quality, and a perfect-signal ceiling, above which none is. Read along the $\kappa$ axis the condition inverts: where local compute is billed, cost binds, matching a recent empirical finding; where it is sunk, on decentralized hardware, feasibility becomes unconditional and signal quality instead sets what the cascade achieves. We turn the condition into three design requirements that existing trained-in primitives satisfy only in isolation, and we propose, as future work, a co-designed architecture and a protocol to test it. The condition and the inversion hold independently of that architecture; they are the paper's cont

61f78805664bdbceec1d3d25.title_original: Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments
61f78805664bdbceec1d3d25.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As agents become more capable, they are moving beyond one-off tasks toward sustained assistance across successive user goals. Such assistance requires agents to discover how unfamiliar environments work, reuse what they learn across tasks, and keep that experience current as environments evolve. Existing benchmarks increasingly study experience reuse and adaptation, but provide limited insight into which parts of accumulated experience agents revise, retain, or lose. To address this gap, we introduce ReScopeBench, a benchmark for the experience lifecycle across 18 interactive environments. It distinguishes structural experience about how an environment is organized and accessed from rule experience about reusable principles and constraints that guide decisions across tasks. To study how experience is acquired, reused, and revised, we propose an experience-first construction approach. It builds task streams around shared experience and introduces silent environmental changes. We evaluate task performance and track changes in saved experience throughout each stream. Across 20 models, we find that retained experience improves task performance, but agents struggle to keep it current as environments change. Even when the required experience is correctly recorded, agents do not always complete tasks successfully. These findings identify selective maintenance and effective use as complementary challenges for long-lived agents.

73237386222131b137efcc8e.title_original: Can Large Language Models Review the Scientific Literature? A Test Against a 102-Article Benchmark
73237386222131b137efcc8e.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support scientific literature reviews, yet evaluations often examine individual tasks rather than the review process as a whole. We assess six AI tools across four stages: finding relevant articles, interpreting them, synthesizing across them, and proposing future research. The benchmark is a published review of the Spanish plume weather pattern and its 102-article corpus. In the initial searches, five tools collectively identified 57 articles, with the best individual tool finding 42. Institutional library access increased discovery from 42 to 82 articles for Codex and from 15 to 79 for Claude Code. Given the complete corpus of 102 PDFs, three tools correctly identified all 18 articles discussing the Spanish plume substantially, but incorrectly classified 40% to 79% of the 84 passing mentions as substantial. The same three tools produced syntheses evaluated blindly by two domain experts. Although largely accurate, the syntheses provided limited insight and sometimes contained unsupported claims, quotation errors, and exaggerated statements of consensus. Finally, all three tools proposed research directions broader than the Spanish plume literature, although two approached questions identified in the benchmark review. No single tool performed best across all tasks. We provide eight recommendations for researchers using AI tools in literature reviews. Our findings suggest that

6540ef6e51f6b64edc395e3e.title_original: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
6540ef6e51f6b64edc395e3e.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI Agents are becoming digital coworkers that can browse the web, write code, run experiments, and assist humans over extended horizons. Yet existing benchmarks fall short of real knowledge work: many rely on synthetic data or isolated tasks, missing the complex, multi-party dynamics of collaborative projects, where critical information is scattered across conversations, code, and evolving decisions. Even simple workplace questions may require locating relevant channels and direct messages, recovering context from long discussions, inspecting repository state, reconciling stale or conflicting evidence, and synthesizing across sources. We introduce SlackBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents on realistic research and engineering workflows that require joint reasoning over workplace communication and evolving repository state. Grounded in privacy-preserving reenactments of real academic research projects, SlackBench provides reproducible environments with realistic multi-party dialogue, evolving decisions, and corresponding code changes grounded in GitHub repositories and Google Docs. It contains 140 queries spanning heterogeneous-source agentic search, abstention on unanswerable or false-premise questions, goal-directed summarization, and circumstance inference over long conversations. 227dde2a7c5ebebcbd5efe82.title_original: MA-SafeDiffuser: Safe Multi-Agent Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models
227dde2a7c5ebebcbd5efe82.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose MA-SafeDiffuser, a multi-agent extension of SafeDiffuser that equips diffusion-based trajectory planners with finite-time diffusion invariance guarantees for joint-agent safety specifications. Building on the single-agent construction that embeds control barrier function (CBF) constraints into reverse-diffusion updates, we: (i) formalize joint safe sets as intersections of per-agent and pairwise barrier sets; (ii) derive centralized and decentralized (communication-aware) constrained denoising procedures with provable invariance under mild assumptions; (iii) address local-trap and deadlock phenomena via time-varying specifications and liveness CBFs; and (iv) develop a lightweight benchmarking suite including a multi-agent Maze2D domain. Empirically, MA-SafeDiffuser reduces violation counts relative to unconstrained diffusion baselines, while retaining planning quality. We provide algorithms, proofs, and reference implementations.

e1b63f792df22a5c8f037506.title_original: Towards Efficient Whole Page Ranking with One-Pass Inference
e1b63f792df22a5c8f037506.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whole-page ranking jointly optimizes advertisements and organic content to balance business outcomes and user engagement under complex layout and business constraints. Existing non-autoregressive (NAR) approaches enable efficient page generation but typically score candidate items independently of previously selected items, limiting their ability to capture order-dependent interactions. Autoregressive (AR) methods address this limitation through sequential conditioning, but incur substantial inference overhead that challenges large-scale deployment. Bridging this quality-efficiency gap remains a challenge in industrial whole-page ranking. We propose Multi-Item Scoring (MIS), a prefix-aware NAR-style framework that incorporates sequential context into efficient multi-item scoring. MIS integrates global candidate interactions, localized prefix conditioning, and position-aware scoring within a shared representation architecture. By computing reusable representations once per request and performing lightweight prefix-conditioned scoring during constrained beam search, MIS captures important sequential dependencies without repeated full-model inference. Experiments on KuaiRand-1K and RL4RS demonstrate that MIS approaches the generation quality of an autoregressive CGA baseline while achieving 4.07x and 3.54x faster CPU decoding, respectively. 1014ad3212cd4766099dab99.title_original: Iterated creation, grading, and revision of data science projects by language models
1014ad3212cd4766099dab99.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluate the extent to which agentic AI models can complete an end-to-end data science project, and how this improves with feedback. A 'writer' model with specific tools creates a complete data science project including downloading, cleaning, and analyzing a dataset, and writing a short paper about it. The project is executed and a 'grader' model evaluates it. The writer can then revise its submission, and this repeats for a total of three rounds. We consider seven models from five developers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and Z.AI. Each model is both a writer and a grader, so there are 49 writer-grader pairs and we run each pair three times. Of the 147 initial submissions, 107 run and render, and the average score increases from 59 per cent to 76 per cent after the final round of feedback. By writer the extent of the increase ranges from 3 percentage points for Anthropic's Opus 5.5 to 46 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5, and by grader it ranges from 13 percentage points for Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash to 32 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5. When a model grades its own writing the score tends to be about 9 percentage points higher than the average of what the other models give it. About half of the difference that we see from round to round is within the grader's own noise. 41173e1c74435666c63bd310.title_original: Whose Transparency is it Anyway? Understanding Generative AI Transparency Needs and Gaps Across Stakeholders
41173e1c74435666c63bd310.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transparency has become a central principle in AI governance, yet there is little agreement about what transparency means, for whom, and in what contexts. Drawing on interpretive flexibility within the Social Construction of Technology, this paper examines how different stakeholders understand and experience transparency in generative AI. This study draws from a global survey of 400 end-users, AI builders, and policymakers, complemented by a structured focus group with end-users, grounding the quantitative findings in qualitative insights from the group most underserved by current transparency practice. We present three key findings. First, all three groups share similar understandings of what transparency means and what it should afford, centered on ensuring accuracy and privacy. Second, gaps between the importance of transparency features and their perceived availability are substantially larger for end-users than builders, revealing how power shapes what gets built and who it serves. Only 28% of end-users report that current transparency practices reflect their needs very well, compared to 53% of builders and 49% of policymakers. Third, transparency is situationally constructed, priorities shift with context and task structure, with role-specific frames activating when context demands them and receding when it does not. We argue that meaningful AI transparency requires moving beyond a one-size-fits-all solution, including cur

2bf7262bfe8b2584cd263657.title_original: VirtualTrialHarness: Coordinating Agentic Operationalization of Virtual Trial Protocols Across Complex Clinical Schemas
2bf7262bfe8b2584cd263657.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Virtual trials use routinely collected clinical data to evaluate treatment strategies, but translating a study protocol into an executable analysis requires determining how clinical concepts and study requirements should be represented in the available data and applied consistently across the workflow. These decisions depend on local data representations and operational conventions and can involve source selection, patient and encounter identity, linkage, and temporal interpretation. Here we introduce VirtualTrialHarness (VTHarness), an agent framework that coordinates virtual-trial operationalization by selecting reusable procedural skills for each workflow stage and uses explicit contracts to maintain consistent study decisions across stages. We also introduce VTBenchmark for evaluating source selection and cohort construction. Across three complex synthetic environments, VTHarness successfully produced all required cohort outputs matching the references in 95.1% of workflows after requirement clarification, compared with 60.4% using retrieval from the same procedural corpus. Procedural skills improved source recovery across three language models and increased source overlap with analyst code in 13 Mayo Clinic cases. Site-specific adaptation enabled reference-matched cohort execution across eight MIMIC-IV tasks. Within the Mayo Clinic Virtual Trials Program, the framework supported investigator review of cohort construction an

55e9ad3b83806ed144c1a279.title_original: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
55e9ad3b83806ed144c1a279.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-as-a-judge is a common substitute for costly human evaluation, and aggregating several judges is the standard remedy for any single judge's bias. Judge pools mix judges of very different reliability, while the human-labeled sets that validate them hold a few hundred items or fewer. In this regime the per-item mean weights weak judges as heavily as strong ones, and confusion-table models such as Dawid-Skene must estimate a per-judge error table from too few items. We propose AGORA (Aggregation Of Reliability-weighted Assessments), an item-response-theory aggregator that places every item on one latent quality scale and describes each judge by a sensitivity parameter and ordered rating thresholds, so judge reliability is learned from all items jointly and without human labels. Across three benchmarks, AGORA matches or exceeds Dawid-Skene on large evaluation sets, and its advantage widens as the set shrinks toward a few hundred items. It remains accurate as pools grow more uneven, a label-free dispersion statistic indicates in advance when trust weighting helps, and its learned trust weights track per-judge human validity.

d7aba140eeaa703707d67ca4.title_original: BrainBind: Bridging Synchronized EEG and fMRI through Long-Form Naturalistic Video Representations
d7aba140eeaa703707d67ca4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world vision is dynamic and scene-rich, while EEG and fMRI resolve it at complementary temporal and spatial scales. Most neural decoding systems, however, align one modality in isolation and mostly against static images or short clips. We study the synchronized case: EEG and fMRI are recorded during the same long-form naturalistic viewing, giving a shared stimulus but also recurring narrative context and many semantically similar candidates. We present BrainBind, a framework that maps synchronized EEG and fMRI into frozen long-form video embedding spaces and treats those spaces as common visual-semantic references, not literal neural codes. On CineBrain, a five-seed Recall@K 2 x 4 matrix across two video anchors and four system configurations shows distinct retrieval profiles. With Omni, fMRI organizes the full candidate list most strongly (MRR = 23.82, nDCG@10 = 25.31), while Joint-Dual gives the highest mean label-aware R@1 (13.52%) with a distinct rank-wide profile. The complementary episode-disjoint evaluation quantifies the contribution of repeated stimulus identity and narrative context to the random split. Across these experiments, proxy choice and system configuration produce distinct top-rank and rank-wide retrieval profiles within the present synchronized dataset. The code is available at https://github.com/Forainest789/Brainbind.

8ac012b93ce7a1017f816d74.title_original: Anduin: A sybil-resistant agentic marketplace reputation system
8ac012b93ce7a1017f816d74.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As autonomous AI agents enter permissionless onchain markets, selecting new service providers remains a core challenge. Existing reputation systems depend on scarce resources like human curation, identity credentials, or voluntary reviews, while naive volume rankings are vulnerable to Sybil attacks. We evaluate whether existing onchain payment histories can yield provider ratings that are resilient against Sybil attacks. Using a 157-day dataset comprising 66M agentic transactions worth $6.1M across 16 blockchains, we model payment flows as a bipartite graph between buyers and providers. A provider's rating is derived from graph paths linked to a buyer's existing trusted network. We propose three Sybil-resistant rating algorithms: a max-flow rating and two relaxed algorithms optimized for stronger rating performance. Evaluating these algorithms against simulated adversaries across 813 buyers, we show that rating manipulation costs 20% of those buyers' total spend and is around 23x harder to manipulate than the standard similarity rule (collaborative filtering).

1e815dbb23fb96f998a0bbcb.excerpt: arXiv:2611.05590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What should ``verified'' mean when evaluating LLM-generated code?
